newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA HPCL 97/98 DEBT AT 500 MLN RUPEES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA HPCL 97/98 DEBT AT 500 MLN RUPEES.

text.p: The net short-term borrowings of state-run Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) in 1997/98 (April-March) amount to 500 million rupees, a top company official said on Friday.
"Our short-term debt from April to August is about 500 million," the official said. He said the bulk of the amount was raised through the issue of commercial papers (CPs).
Many analysts believe the borrowings would be much larger than 500 million rupees.
Dues owed to the company from the oil pool account, which manages the government's oil subsidy, amounted to 6.50 billion rupees for the year ended March 1997, the official said.
He did not give figure for dues owed this year.
The official denied reports in some newspapers that HPCL planned to raise offshore debt.
"We have no concrete plan for an ECB (external commercial borrowing)," he said.
